source_span: Brent trades at $96, but the six-month contract sits near $83 as the curve continues to price a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz... If the blockage persists, the back end will eventually have to adjust higher, removing an important source of support for equities and credit.
source_chain: The oil futures curve is downward-sloping because the market is pricing an eventual Strait of Hormuz reopening (front ~$96 vs 6-month ~$83) THEREFORE that reopening has been expected and dashed for six months running THEREFORE the pricing is an unsustainable bet rather than a settled fact, so if the blockage persists the 6-month (back-end) price must rise to meet reality, removing a support pillar under equities and credit. Invalidation: a real, sustained reopening of the strait — that would vindicate the curve's current pricing instead of forcing it higher.
pulse_chain: The forward curve is priced for a Hormuz reopening that hasn't arrived in six months (Brent ~$97 spot vs $83.20 six-month) THEREFORE the market's bet has repeatedly been wrong THEREFORE the gap must resolve one of two ways by the time the six-month contract rolls (~March): downward if the strait genuinely reopens, or upward (with $USO rising) if it doesn't. Invalidation: a sustained reopening of the strait.
why: The pulse reproduces DB's exact mechanism and direction (unresolved curve mispricing forces the back end higher absent a reopening) and its exact invalidation (a real reopening), just left uncredited to DB and padded with corroborating Goldman/JPMorgan detail rather than a swapped or invented mechanism.
